title: Oussama Batouche väittelee aiheesta Laskennalliset menetelmät eturauhassyövän profilointiin ja hoitotulosten ennustamiseen
content:
M.Sc. Abderrahim Oussama Batouche defends his PhD thesis “Computational Methods for Prostate Cancer Profiling and Outcome Prediction” on Thursday the 26th of November 2026 at 13 in the University of Helsinki Main Building, Auditorium Karolina Eskelin (U3032, Unioninkatu 34, 3rd floor). His opponent is Professor Arto Mannermaa (University of Eastern Finland) and custos Professor Arto Klami (University of Helsinki). The defence will be held in English.

The thesis of Abderrahim Oussama Batouche is a part of research done in the Department of Computer Science and in the Helsinki Urological Cancer Center (HUCC) at the Faculty of Medicine. His supervisors have been Professor Antti Rannikko, University Researcher Tuomas Mirtti and University Researcher Eugen Czeizler (University of Helsinki).

title: Helsingin yliopiston johtamalle konsortiolle 10 miljoonan euron ERC Synergy-rahoitus ihmisen perimän salaisuuksien tutkimiseen
content:
An international consortium led by Professor Sakari Vanharanta and Professor Lauri Aaltonen from the University of Helsinki (Finland), Professor Jussi Taipale from the Wellcome Sanger Institute (UK) and Professor Carl de Boer from the University of British Columbia (Canada) has been awarded a prestigious European Research Council (ERC) Synergy Grant for the project FIBERMAP. The consortium receives a total of around €10 million, of which around €4.5 million goes to the University of Helsinki's subprojects.

The ERC Synergy Grant is among Europe’s most competitive and highly regarded research funding instruments, supporting small groups of outstanding researchers whose complementary expertise enables them to tackle the most challenging scientific questions. The FIBERMAP consortium brings together world-leading expertise in high-throughput biochemistry, human genomics, computational biology and cancer research.

title: Samuel Singler ja Anne-Marie Houde ovat uudet yhteiskunnallisen turvallisuuden ohjelman yliopistonlehtorit
content:
The first students of the Master's programme in Societal Security will begin their studies in autumn 2027, and two new university lecturers have already been recruited during the spring and autumn. The recruitment of the third university lecturer is currently underway. 

The planning of the programme teaching is also actively progressing. The work will not end when the first students begin their studies.  

– Research-based teaching also relies heavily on student feedback, which can influence the content and themes of my research, so I'm looking forward to discussing and exchanging ideas with the security experts of the future, says . 

Singler's earlier research themes have dealt especially with surveillance technologies and their security-policy dimensions. He is responsible for the programmes Economic Structures, Technological Change, and Crises –study track. 

Singler earned his PhD from the University of Oxford in 2022. Among other roles at Oxford, he has previously worked as a university lecturer. He also has experience working at the University of Essex, where he served as an assistant professor.

title: New Master’s Programme in One Health to train experts for health threats that cross disciplines and borders
content:
“Covid made me realise how little I actually knew about other fields,” says Tarja Sironen, Professor of Emerging Infectious Diseases at the University of Helsinki.

During the pandemic, virologists like Sironen suddenly had to work with social scientists, lawyers and physicists. Even explaining how the virus spread through the air required expertise from several disciplines at once.

The pandemic also showed how quickly a health threat can grow into an economic and societal crisis, and how much trust can be lost along the way. Ministries have since said openly that they wish experts capable of working across disciplines already existed. Few graduates today are trained for such work. The new Master’s Programme in One Health, launching at the University of Helsinki in autumn 2027, aims to close this gap.

Unlike most health-related master’s programmes, the new programme will bring together students and researchers from six faculties. After learning the foundations in One Health, students will choose their focus from eight thematic areas, such as infectious disease dynamics, food and water safety, environmental health, or governance and policy.

title: ANEE+ employed researchers starting work
content: The call for applications for postdoctoral and university researcher positions in the study of ancient Near East received a large number of high-quality proposals. The ANEE+ management team is excited to announce that Emanuel Pfoh and Melis Uzdurum were chosen for university researcher positions, and Ellie Bennett and Richard Bott for postdoctoral researcher positions. These four new hires strengthen the role of ancient Near Eastern studies at the University of Helsinki and further the goals of the ANEE+ Interdisciplinary Research Network.

title: Luonnontieteellisen museon Elämän historia -sali sulkeutuu tammikuussa – uusi näyttely avautuu loppuvuodesta 2028
content:
The Natural History Museum’s History of Life is one of the museum’s most popular exhibitions. However, the exhibition, completed in 2008, has long been in need of an update, as it is outdated both in terms of content and exhibition technology.

– The new exhibition will present evolution and the development of biodiversity in a more spectacular and tangible way than before. This is the museum’s most significant renewal project in years, says Sanna Vuori, Head of the Public Engagement Unit at the Finnish Museum of Natural History.

The dinosaurs Giganotosaurus carolinii and Shunosaurus lii in the History of Life exhibition have become familiar to many museum visitors over the years. They will remain in the new exhibition but will be joined by never-before-seen reconstructions of prehistoric animals. Among other things, a reconstruction of the otter-like early whale Ambulocetus natans is currently being built in the museum’s conservation facilities.

title: Southnord Artfest 2026: Roots en Route
content:
Plants have always travelled – with the wind, with animals and birds, with humans. They have been carried across oceans, taken from their habitats and replanted to serve trade and empire.

Roots en Route is a multi-sensory installation by four artists who will create a multi-sensory installation in dialogue with the greenhouses – examining rootedness and displacement; asking what grows where it was planted and what survives the crossing. The African plants that fill the greenhouses carry their own histories of movement and adaptation.

Camille Norment in collaboration with Sofia Jernberg create a soundscape drawing on the insects and birds of the plants' homelands. Toubab Holmes' site-specific scent installation traces the hidden journeys of plants through the extractive system of perfumery. Charmaine Watkiss visits the botanical legacies and healing traditions of her Caribbean ancestry through large-scale drawings of Plant Warriors. Together, the three works read the botanical garden as an archive of movement, and the plants in it as things that were carried, taken and made to travel.

title: “Ilman pölyttäjiä maailma olisi ankea ja väritön” – Uusi näyttely avaa oven pölyttäjien kiehtovaan elämään
content:
Pollinators represent an astonishingly diverse group of animals, many of which possess remarkable abilities despite their small size. Bees can count, bumblebees solve problems, and on distant islands, even lizards can pollinate flowers.

The  exhibition, which combines science and art, offers a wealth of information, stunning visuals, and fun activities for visitors of all ages. Guests can play interactive games like "Identify the Pollinators" and "Pollinator Protection Bingo," design their own imaginary pollinator, and explore the museum's impressive collection of specimens. The exhibition is based on a newly illustrated non-fiction book.

– We want to show the world through the eyes of pollinators, says exhibition scriptwriter Mia Rönkä, Adjunct Professor in Environmental Ecology at the University of Turku. Rönkä has written the exhibition’s informational texts and poems.

Although the sensory perceptions, cognitive abilities, and communication methods of pollinators like bees differ from ours as humans, we can still strive to understand and appreciate them as individuals of other species – without anthropomorphizing them, Rönkä explains.

title: Ukrainan sota - yliopiston suositukset
content:
The University of Helsinki has condemned the military action by Russia and expressed its support for Ukraine and its university community. We have also expressed our support for Ukraine, together with other Finnish universities, through statements by and the . As a demonstration of support, we have illuminated buildings in the colours of the Ukrainian flag and raised the flag on our premises.

One of the principles of the University of Helsinki is to promote international collaboration in research and higher education, and to support these efforts even in difficult circumstances. Russia’s indefensible military aggression in Ukraine has required exceptional measures, which include those taken in the collaboration between universities.

The University of Helsinki is monitoring both national and EU-level sanctions, adapting our policies and processes accordingly. Together with other Finnish and international universities, the University of Helsinki strives to promote the end of military action in Ukraine, while supporting Ukrainian institutions and people.

title: Markku Kulmala named honorary doctor of the Estonian University of Life Sciences
content:
His work centres on how very small particles, called aerosols, are formed in the atmosphere. He studies how these particles affect both air quality and the climate. Kulmala has also made major contributions to understanding how the atmosphere and ecosystems interact.

He is one of the most highly cited geoscientists in the world. The university honours its honorary doctors at an academic ceremony.

title: Miten pelloille ja laitumille saadaan lisää elämää?
content: I pursue a better understanding of the factors that maintain biodiversity in agriculture and explain organismal community composition and the ecosystem services they produce, including pollination and natural pest control. In particular, I have investigated ecological processes that explain how changes in land use and landscape structure together affect biodiversity in agriculture. I am also particularly interested in integrating ecology and biodiversity research into broader cross-disciplinary contexts.
